ONE QUOTE. THE WHOLE JOURNEY.

Inside BlueMint.

Your token. A USDC market. A dedicated vault that puts collected fees back into liquidity.

BlueMint is a USDC-first launchpad on Solana. The launch flow creates a standard SPL token and a direct Raydium CPMM pool. It does not use a LaunchLab bonding curve or require a graduation stage.

MAINNET ACTIVATION PENDING

The site and launch profiles are available. On-chain launches and automated liquidity execution remain disabled until deployment and operational checks pass. This guide describes the implemented flow awaiting activation; animations are illustrations.

Create a launch profileExplore The Mint
02 / FROM IDEA TO MARKET

Three wallet steps.

First, connect on the launch page and save your token name, ticker, PFP and official links. Saving a public profile does not mint a token or move money. When launches are enabled, each transaction is reviewed in your wallet.

01

Mint

Create the fixed-supply SPL token. Mint authority is revoked and freeze authority is absent.

02

Seed

Half your USDC budget and the full token supply seed the Raydium pool. The other half stays in your token’s vault for the initial purchase.

03

Buy

Once the pool opens, the reserved USDC buys tokens for your wallet. Finalized on-chain checks confirm the completed launch.

Example: a 100 USDC developer budget

50 USDC seeds liquidity. The remaining 50 USDC funds the developer purchase. SOL is required separately for rent, pool creation and transaction fees. There is no separate liquidity-commitment field.

The first purchase can receive roughly half the token supply. The pool becomes public when it opens, so other traders can trade before your purchase completes. If the initial buy expires after 15 minutes, the owner can reclaim only its unspent USDC; the seeded pool liquidity stays in place.

Profile details are fixed in BlueMint’s registry. On-chain metadata points to server-hosted content; an immutable URI is not the same as permanent, content-addressed file storage.

03 / THE QUOTE ASSET

Every pool, paired with USDC.

The launch token is the base asset and Circle USDC on Solana is the quote asset. Prices, market caps, budgets and liquidity values are displayed in USDC. SOL pays network costs; it is not the pool’s quote currency.

USDC mint · Solana mainnet

Use the mint address to identify the quote asset, not a ticker or logo alone. Pairing with USDC does not make the launched token stable or guarantee its price. Liquidity depth, trade size and market activity still affect execution.

04 / FOLLOW THE FEES

A 1.25% launchpad fee.

The configured launchpad creator fee is 1.25%, in addition to Raydium trading fees. The implementation requires CPMM configuration 20 with an expected 0.25% trading fee and 1.25% creator fee, collected on the USDC side. Configuration checks must pass before transactions are prepared.

AllocationHeadline rateActual distribution
Launchpad treasury0.50%40% of net creator fees received
Token’s liquidity vault0.75%60% of net creator fees received
Raydium trading fee0.25% expectedSeparate from the creator-fee split

Raydium deducts its protocol share from creator fees before BlueMint receives them. This means the treasury and liquidity vault receive less than the headline 0.50% and 0.75% of trading value. The split is applied to actual receipts: for every 100 USDC received after that deduction, 40 goes to the launchpad treasury and 60 remains allocated to that token’s liquidity.

Price impact, slippage, SOL network costs and any terminal charges are separate. Review the transaction quote before signing. There are no holder rewards or automatic holder distributions.

05 / TWO DIFFERENT DESTINATIONS

Treasury is not token liquidity.

Launchpad treasury

Receives 40% of net collected creator fees. This is the platform’s allocation, separate from each token’s reinvestment budget.

Per-token vault

Holds that token’s pending USDC, assets used for reinvestment, and LP tokens. Each token has independent vault accounts.

Configured treasury address

85a8ERAhk1ZPYyGwj4zkjVKZdfqaEUcSpTt9GCz5xA7j

The current vault contract exposes no arbitrary asset-transfer, LP-withdrawal or treasury-redirection instruction. However, a program upgrade authority can change program behavior. Vault custody should not be described as an irrevocable liquidity lock while upgrades remain possible.

06 / BUY. PAIR. STACK.

How The Mint deepens liquidity.

  1. Collect: creator fees are collected from the token’s Raydium pool and split into treasury and token-liquidity allocations.
  2. Buy: a bounded part of the liquidity budget buys tokens from that same pool.
  3. Pair: purchased tokens are paired with retained USDC.
  4. Deposit: both assets are added to the pool and the resulting LP tokens remain in the vault.

A keeper submits the operations and pays SOL network fees. It cannot choose a new destination for vault assets. This is periodic execution, not a guaranteed immediate reinvestment after each trade.

Execution bounds

Each batch is capped at 0.1% of quote reserves. The program requires a fresh 15–30 minute price-observation window, spot price within 3% of that observation price, and 0.5% swap slippage. If conditions fail or history is missing, funds stay pending.

More liquidity can reduce price impact for a given trade size, but does not establish a price floor, prevent selling or guarantee returns. The treasury animation illustrates the process; it is not a live balance counter.

07 / DISCOVERY & DATA

Standard pools. Transparent data.

Direct Raydium CPMM pools are intended to work through compatible trading routes. Discovery and support on Axiom or other terminals are controlled by those providers; BlueMint cannot guarantee immediate indexing or support on every terminal.

The market-data implementation samples finalized pool reserves into one-minute OHLC observations. These are reserve-price observations, not a complete history of individual swaps. Missing intervals are not filled with invented candles. Trade-level history and 24-hour trading volume are not yet indexed.

Sample markets and animations are labeled as illustrative. A draft profile is not proof that a token has minted or that its pool is live.

08 / BEFORE MAINNET LAUNCHES OPEN

What still needs activation.

The vault must be deployed at the configured program address and its binary verified. A separate funded keeper and scheduler must be configured. Launches are enabled only after readiness checks pass and an owner-reviewed mainnet launch verifies the complete flow.

Local contract integration tests have passed. That is not an independent security audit. Wallet signing stays with the user; BlueMint does not ask for a seed phrase or private key.
